name: RoboShuttle V5
summary: Geek+ tote-to-person warehouse system pairing rail and mobile case-handling robots with an AI robot-arm picking station for unmanned fulfillment.
note: Scope flag: RoboShuttle V5 is a tote-to-person SYSTEM, not a single robot - it combines rail-mounted RS Air robots (up to 4 m/s, i.e. not free-roaming), mobile RS case-handling robots (ACRs), P40 transport AMRs and a Robot Arm Picking Station (RAPS, up to 700 UPH, 99.99% accuracy). Launched at LogiMAT, 24 Mar 2026. Storage up to 12 m; totes 350x270x120 to 850x650x500 mm; >5,000 robots per deployment. No per-robot dimensions/payload/speed in the release, so robot specs left out; consider cataloguing the RS-series ACR or P40 instead. Geek+ (Geekplus Technology Co., Beijing; HKEX 2590).
misc_reason: Warehouse system combining several robot types; no single-robot specs.

name: Xiao Nuo (AI robotic head)
summary: Stationary lifelike robotic head with 32 active DoF facial expressions and LLM voice interaction for reception and companionship (not a mobile robot).
note: MAJOR CORRECTION: official page title is 'Xiao Nuo AI Robotic Head' - it is a stationary biomimetic robotic HEAD/bust (32 active + 8 passive DoF facial expression) with no locomotion, not a mobile humanoid. Recommend removing from the mobile-robot catalog. Docs link names it 'Hobbs 3'. Cross-platform SDK, joint-control/face/lip-sync APIs.

name: ALLEX
summary: WIRobotics' compliant general-purpose humanoid upper body with force-sensitive 15-DoF hands, currently without legs or a mobile base.
note: OUT OF SCOPE (not mobile): WIRobotics' own spec table states 'General-purpose humanoid robot upper body (Currently without lower body)'. Maker states hand/arm 15 DoF (English RIH page typo '115DOF'), >3 kg per hand, hook grip >30 kg, hand ~700 g, below-shoulder ~5 kg. Aggregator values (1650 mm, 55 kg, 43 DoF, 1.2 m/s, 120 min) are not maker-stated and were ignored. Unveiled Aug 2025 (press release). Category 'Humanoid' is fine but locomotion n/a.
misc_reason: Upper body only; maker says no lower body yet.

name: iRonCub3
summary: IIT's experimental jet-powered humanoid that combines iCub walking and manipulation with turbine flight for future disaster-response research.
note: Research platform, not a product: jet-powered flying humanoid built on iCub3 with four jet turbines (two on arms, two on a back jetpack); first liftoff ~50 cm reported in IIT press release 18 Jun 2025. Maker states iRonCub MK3 with jet engines weighs about 70 kg and turbines give >1000 N max thrust. Locomotion is legged (iCub walking base) plus aerial flight — no catalog category fits cleanly; consider out-of-scope for a mobile-robot catalog. Uses onboard IMU and RealSense camera for pose estimation.

name: CODiAQ
summary: AI-targeted weapon kit on a Ghost Robotics Vision 60 quadruped that gives small special-operations units remote direct-fire and breaching capability.
note: Scope/identity flag: CODiAQ is an armed 'lethality kit' (Skyborne targeting box + HAVOC 40mm / CHAOS 12GA weapon) integrated on a Ghost Robotics Vision 60 quadruped; the walking platform is Ghost Robotics', not Skyborne's - risk of duplicating Vision 60 in the catalogue. Datasheet: 66 kg operational mass (with HAVOC), <=2 h 15 min runtime, 10.5 km/h (2.92 m/s), IP67, MIL-STD-810H, TRL 8, ATEC safety release; 14 systems delivering to SOF (maker one-pager excerpt). Status Pilot (operational test & combat evaluation). Country left out: datasheet lists Virginia USA + Brisbane AU.
misc_reason: Weapon payload kit mounted on Ghost Robotics Vision 60; not a separate robot.

name: Ameca
summary: Engineered Arts' expressive social humanoid for museums, events and human-robot interaction research, sold or rented on quote.
note: Maker spec page (engineeredarts.com/robots/ameca/specs): 1870 mm high, 470 mm wide, 850 mm deep, 62 kg, 61 actuated DoF (27 head, 5 neck, 8 shoulders, 10 arms and the rest of the upper body), first release 2021, generation 2.6 shown in 2024. Fixed base, no legs and no drive: it cannot walk, so it is not a standalone mobile robot and does not fit a catalog category. Price is quote-only (purchase or rental); the maker publishes no figure.
misc_reason: Fixed-base social humanoid — cannot walk and has no drive, so it is not a standalone mobile robot.

name: Realbotix Series 1
summary: Realbotix's human-likeness companion and reception humanoid, sold as a tabletop (17 DoF) or full-body (39 DoF) unit with a monthly AI plan.
note: Maker site and its own shop (realbotix.com, shop.realbotix.com): two sizes — full body 39 DoF, 72 in (female) / 77 in (male) tall and 88 lb, and tabletop 17 DoF, 31-32 in tall and 25 lb; height_mm 1830 and weight_kg 40 are the full-body figures converted from the maker's imperial ones (72 in x 25.4, 88 lb / 2.205), and the maker calls sizes and weights approximate. Powered from a standard wall outlet with no battery, so it is fixed in place: not a standalone mobile robot and not a catalog category. Line launched for pre-order on 2026-10-27 as Echo and renamed Series 1 on 2026-11-04; delivery is stated for the second half of 2027, and a monthly AI plan is required. Maker-stated prices are not recorded here because market price fields await the owner's schema review on issue #74.
misc_reason: Fixed-base companion humanoid run from mains power — not a standalone mobile robot.
